1.1: Sha’ul and Timotiyos, servants of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, to all the qodeshim in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 who are in Philippi, with the overseers and attendants:
1.2: Favor to you and peace from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Father and the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ.
1.3: I thank my Elohim in all my remembrance of you.
1.4: In all my prayers for all of you, I always pray with joy,
1.5: for your fellowship in the Good News from the first day until now,
1.6: being persuaded of this, that He who has begun a good work in you shall perfect it until the day of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ.
1.7: It is right for me to think this of you all, because I have you in my heart, all of you being sharers of the favor with me, both in my chains and in the defense and confirmation of the Good News.
1.8: For Elohim is my witness, how I long for you all with the affection of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ.
1.9: And this I pray, that your love might extend more and more in knowledge and all discernment,
1.10: for you to examine those that differ, in order to be sincere, and not stumbling, until the day of Mashiaḥ,
1.11: being filled with the fruit of righteousness, through 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, to the esteem and praise of Elohim.
1.12: And I want you to know, brothers, that what has befallen me has turned out for the advancement of the Good News,
1.13: so that it has become known to all the palace guard, and to all the rest, that my chains are in Mashiaḥ;
1.14: and most of the brothers, trusting in the Aḏon because of my chains, are much more bold to fearlessly speak the Word.
1.15: Some indeed proclaim Mashiaḥ even from envy and strife, but some also out of goodwill -
1.16: the former announce Mashiaḥ from selfish ambition, not sincerely, thinking to add distress to my chains,
1.17: but the latter out of love, knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the Good News.
1.18: What then? Only that in every way, whether in pretense or in truth, Mashiaḥ is announced. And in this I rejoice, in fact, I shall rejoice.
1.19: For I know that this shall turn out for my deliverance through your prayer and the supply of the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ,
1.20: according to my intense longing and anticipation that I shall not be ashamed at all, but that with all boldness, as always, so now also Mashiaḥ shall be made great in my body, whether by life or by death.
1.21: For to me, to live is Mashiaḥ, and to die is gain.
1.22: And if to live in the flesh is to me a fruit of work, then what shall I choose? I do not know.
1.23: For I am pressed down by the two, having a desire to depart and be with Mashiaḥ, which is much better,
1.24: but to remain in the flesh is more necessary for your sake.
1.25: And being persuaded of this, I know that I shall stay and continue with you all, for your progress and joy of belief,
1.26: so that your boasting might overflow in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ on account of me, through my coming to you again.
1.27: Only, behave yourselves worthily of the Good News of Mashiaḥ, in order that whether I come and see you or am absent, I hear about you, that you stand fast in one spirit, with one being, striving together for the belief of the Good News,
1.28: without being frightened in any way by those who oppose, which to them truly is a proof of destruction, but to you of deliverance, and that from Elohim.
1.29: Because to you it has been given as a favor, on behalf of Mashiaḥ, not only to believe in Him, but also to suffer for His sake,
1.30: having the same struggle which you saw in me, and now hear to be in me.

2.1: If, then, there is any encouragement in Mashiaḥ, if any comfort of love, if any fellowship of Ruaḥ, if any affection and compassion,
2.2: make my joy complete by being of the same mind, having the same love, one in being and of purpose,
2.3: doing naught through selfishness or self-conceit, but in humility consider others better than yourselves.
2.4: Each one should look out not only for his own interests, but also for the interests of others.
2.5: For, let this mind be in you which was also in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏,
2.6: who, being in the form of Elohim, did not regard equality with Elohim a matter to be grasped,
2.7: but emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant, and came to be in the likeness of men.
2.8: And having been found in fashion as a man, He humbled Himself and became obedient unto death, death even of a stake.
2.9: Elohim, therefore, has highly exalted Him and given Him the Name which is above every name,
2.10: that at the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 every knee should bow, of those in the shamayim, and of those on earth, and of those under the earth,
2.11: and every tongue should confess that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ is Aḏon, to the esteem of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Father.
2.12: So that, my beloved, as you always obeyed - not only in my presence, but now much rather in my absence - work out your own deliverance with fear and trembling,
2.13: for it is Elohim who is working in you both to desire and to work for well-pleasing.
2.14: Do all without grumblings and disputings,
2.15: in order that you be blameless and faultless, children of Elohim without blemish in the midst of a crooked and corrupt generation, among whom you shine as lights in the world,
2.16: holding on to the Word of ḥai, for a boast to me in the day of Mashiaḥ, that I have not run in vain or labored in vain.
2.17: In fact, even if I am being poured out as a drink offering on the offering and service of your belief, I am glad and rejoice with you all.
2.18: So you too should be glad and rejoice with me.
2.19: But I trust in the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 to send Timotiyos to you shortly, so that I too am encouraged by news from you.
2.20: For I have no one of the same mind, who takes a genuine interest in your welfare.
2.21: For all seek their own, not those of Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
2.22: But you know he has proven himself, that as a son with his father he served with me for the Good News.
2.23: So I expect to send him as soon as I see how it goes with me,
2.24: and I trust in the Aḏon that I myself shall also come shortly.
2.25: But I thought it necessary to send to you Epaphroditos, my brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier, and your emissary and servant to my need,
2.26: since he was longing for you all, and being troubled because you had heard that he was sick.
2.27: For indeed he was sick, near to death, but Elohim had compassion on him, and not only on him but on me as well, lest I should have sadness upon sadness.
2.28: Therefore I sent him more eagerly, so that on seeing him again you might rejoice, and I be less sad.
2.29: Receive him therefore in the Aḏon with all joy, and hold such as he in esteem,
2.30: because for the work of Mashiaḥ he was near death, risking his life, to fill up what was lacking in your service toward me.

3.1: For the rest, my brothers, rejoice in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. To write the same to you is truly no trouble to me, and for you it is safe.
3.2: Look out for dogs, look out for the evil workers, look out for the mutilation!
3.3: For we are the circumcision, who are serving Elohim in the Ruaḥ, and boasting in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, and do not trust in the flesh,
3.4: though I too might have trust in the flesh. If anyone else thinks to trust in the flesh, I more -
3.5: circumcised the eighth day, of the race of Yisra’ĕl, of the tribe of Binyamin, an Iḇri of Iḇrim, according to Torah a Pharisee,
3.6: according to ardor, persecuting the assembly; according to righteousness that is in the law, having become blameless.
3.7: But whatever things were gain to me, I have counted as loss, because of Mashiaḥ,
3.8: What is more, I even count all to be loss because of the excellence of the knowledge of Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 Aḏonai, for whom I have suffered the loss of all, and count them as refuse, in order to gain Mashiaḥ,
3.9: and be found in Him, not having my own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through belief in Mashiaḥ, the righteousness which is from Elohim on the basis of belief,
3.10: to know Him, and the power of His resurrection, and the fellowship of His sufferings, being conformed to His death,
3.11: if somehow I might attain to the resurrection out from the dead.
3.12: Not that I have already received, or already been perfected, but I press on, to lay hold of that for which Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 has also laid hold of me.
3.13: Brothers, I do not count myself to have laid hold of it yet, but only this: forgetting what is behind and reaching out for what lies ahead,
3.14: I press on toward the goal for the prize of the high calling of Elohim in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
3.15: As many, then, as are perfect, let us have this mind. And if you think differently in any respect, Elohim shall also reveal this to you.
3.16: But to what we have attained - walk by the same rule, be of the same mind.
3.17: Become joint imitators of me, brothers, and regard those who so walk, as you have us for a pattern.
3.18: For many - of whom I have often told you, and now say to you even weeping - walk as enemies of the stake of Mashiaḥ.
3.19: Their end is destruction, their mighty one is their stomach, and their esteem is in their shame - they mind the earthly.
3.20: For our citizenship is in the shamayim, from which we also eagerly wait for the Savior, the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ,
3.21: who shall change our lowly body, to be conformed to His esteemed body, according to the working by which He is able even, to bring all under His control.

4.1: So then, my brothers, beloved and longed-for, my joy and crown, stand firm thus in the Aḏon, beloved.
4.2: I appeal to Euodia and I appeal to Suntuḵĕ to be of the same mind in the Aḏon.
4.3: And I also ask you, true companion, help these women who labored with me in the Good News, with Klĕmĕs also, and the rest of my fellow workers, whose names are in the Book of Ḥai.
4.4: Rejoice in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 always, again I say, rejoice!
4.5: Let your gentleness be known to all men. The Aḏon is near.
4.6: Worry for naught, but in all, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to Elohim.
4.7: And the peace of Elohim, which surpasses all understanding, shall guard your hearts and minds through Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
4.8: For the rest, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is noble, whatever is righteous, whatever is clean, whatever is lovely, whatever is of good report, if there is any uprightness and if there is any praise - think on these.
4.9: And what you have learned and received and heard and saw in me, practice these, and the Elohim of peace shall be with you.
4.10: And I rejoiced in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 greatly that now at last your concern for me has revived again - though you were concerned, but had no chance.
4.11: Not that I speak concerning need, for I have learned to be content in whatever state I am.
4.12: I know what it is to be humbled, and I know what it is to have in excess. In any and all, I have learned both to be filled, and to be hungry, both to have in excess, and to be in need.
4.13: I have strength to do all, through Mashiaḥ who empowers me.
4.14: Yet you did well in sharing in my pressure.
4.15: And you know too, Pilipiyim, that in the beginning of the Good News, when I went out from Makedonia, no assembly shared with me concerning giving and receiving, except you only,
4.16: because, even in Thessalonikĕ you sent to my need, once and twice.
4.17: Not that I seek the gift, but I seek the fruit that is multiplying to your account.
4.18: Indeed I have all and more than enough. I have been filled, having received from Epaphroditos what you sent, a sweet-smelling fragrance, an acceptable offering, well-pleasing to Elohim.
4.19: And my Elohim shall fill all your need according to His riches in esteem by Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
4.20: And to our Elohim and Father be esteem forever and ever. Amĕn.
4.21: Greet every qodeshi in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏. The brothers with me greet you.
4.22: All the qodeshim greet you, but most of all those of Kaisar’s household.
4.23: The favor of our Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ be with you all. Amĕn.
